the Casimir energy of a dilute ball at zero temperature is given by the formula: E = - pi^2/720 R^3 (1/lambda^3 - 1/2 lambda), where lambda = (4pi/3) epsilon R^3 is the dielectric constant of the ball, epsilon is the dielectric susceptibility of the material of the ball, R is its radius.

the Casimir energy and pressure of the electromagnetic field in the vacuum in the background of an isolated, dielectric, nonmagnetic, spherical particle of a radius a and dielectric permittivity epsilon at zero temperature is given by the expression E_C = -pi/12 a^3 (epsilon-1)^2, P_C = 1/8 pi a^4 (epsilon-1)(epsilon^2-1).
